thesis_text:
Bottom line: for Duolingo, Inc. (SWE, entry), your odds through the cold application alone are low, but not zero. This read rests on a curated-qualitative record as of 2026-10-12 with no population sample — treat every pattern below as reported, not measured. Craft + collaboration bar rather than a pure algorithm gauntlet: Duolingo officially evaluates for excellence in craft, leadership and citizenship, and its loop tests whether you can work in other people's code (pair programming on a production-like codebase, and a dedicated code-review round) - rounds most big-tech loops do not have.

Who gets in (sample N=not available — curated-qualitative record, as of 2026-10-12):
- This CIR is curated-qualitative: no population sample exists for it yet, so there are no percentages to show. What follows is the reported pattern from public sources, labeled as such.
Known biases of this data: Public postings describe the roles a company is currently trying to fill, not the people it actually hired; interview-prep and review sites are self-selected candidate reports; no licensed population dataset (PDL/Coresignal-class) was available for this record, so no school/employer/major shares are stated. Duolingo-specific: the Thrive posting fetched is the Summer 2025 cycle, so its dates/deadline are historical evidence of cadence, not a current window; Glassdoor intern sample (21 reports) is small and self-selected.. We see who got in, not who tried and failed — survivorship bias is real (§0).

What Duolingo, Inc. says it screens for vs what the record shows:
Stated: Python-or-Java readiness: the official guide advises familiarity with reading/writing Python or Java even if it is not your preferred language Thrive screens: second-year status, 2+ CS courses, transcript upload, ability to relocate to Pittsburgh for 10 weeks; a 3.5+ GPA and a Duolingo learning streak are listed as 'exceptional candidate' signals, not minimums Mission dedication is an explicit Thrive criterion ('dedication to our mission of accessible education') and the careers page frames hiring around the education mission
Revealed: 

Routes in, ranked for you:
First: Thrive internship (second-years; mission/access framing in the programme description) — See route details.
Second: SWE internship (regular) -> new-grad — See route details.
Third: Direct new-grad / industry application via careers page — See route details.

Your gap analysis (highest-leverage fix first: experience):
- school: you — not on file | cohort — See the school pattern in this CIR — stated qualitatively unless the CIR is population-backed; school is not in the user's control, so the plan routes around it (§3.1). | gap | fix: Do not plan around changing schools; offset with experience, projects and referrals.
- experience: you — no internships yet | cohort — Craft + collaboration bar rather than a pure algorithm gauntlet: Duolingo officially evaluates for excellence in craft, leadership and citizenship, and its loop tests whether you can work in other people's code (pair programming on a production-like codebase, and a dedicated code-review round) - rounds most big-tech loops do not have. | gap | fix: Land one real internship or role at a smaller, reachable employer first — the ladder pattern in this CIR's path patterns.
- projects: you — no projects on file | cohort — Revealed screen in this CIR: evidence of building or analyzing real things (see screening_signals.revealed). | gap | fix: Ship one project that solves a messy real problem for a real user, and document it.
- skills: you — no skills on file | cohort — not on file | unknown
- timing: you — year not on file | cohort — Thrive runs on an annual fall application window in the sourced cycle (deadline Oct 10, 2024 for Summer 2025; 10 weeks, mid-June to mid-August) - date-stamped and stale-prone, re-verify each September. Industry/new-grad postings are rolling via the careers page. | unknown
- authorization: you — not on file | cohort — Sponsorship history is a matter of public record (DOL H-1B LCA filings); this CIR states only what its sources support, and immigration specifics go to the school's international office (§4.8 Q26 — not legal advice). | gap | fix: Confirm sponsorship for this exact role family before investing a season of prep; target employers with a filing history for the role.

The plan:
Next thirty days:
- Confirm this cycle's application window and deadlines for Duolingo, Inc. on the official careers page — dates move, and this CIR's cadence fact is the starting point, not the truth (§3.3). (by 2026-10-19)
- Apply to a first, reachable rung: a smaller employer in the same role family (the ladder pattern in this CIR's path patterns). Volume plus follow-up is the play. (by 2026-10-26)
- Ship the first version of one real project and write it up publicly. (by 2026-11-11)
- Build the coffee-chat target list from this CIR's entry routes: recent hires in the same role family, alumni of your school, people one rung up the ladder. (by 2026-10-22)
This semester:
- Convert the semester into signal: one internship or substantial project, one visible leadership or club role in the field, and interview reps on a weekly schedule.
- Run the coffee-chat list: short, specific asks; every conversation ends with a follow-up you actually send.
This year:
- Be in the application pool for Duolingo, Inc.'s main entry window with the ladder rung, the project write-up and the referral conversations already done — not started.
- If the direct route misses, take the highest adjacent rung this CIR names and re-aim with a year of signal (the risks-and-alternatives route in this thesis).

Coffee-chat strategy: target the profile types named in the ranked routes — recent hires in this role family, alumni of your school now inside, and people one rung up the ladder you are climbing. Ask what the interviews actually test, what surprised them after starting, and what they would do with a semester to prepare. Keep asks short and specific; send the follow-up you promised.

Timeline and key dates: Thrive runs on an annual fall application window in the sourced cycle (deadline Oct 10, 2024 for Summer 2025; 10 weeks, mid-June to mid-August) - date-stamped and stale-prone, re-verify each September. Industry/new-grad postings are rolling via the careers page. (as of 2026-10-12; recruiting dates shift every cycle — re-check the official careers page before acting, §3.3).

Risks and alternatives: Language trap: interviewing in a language outside the accepted set (or without Python/Java reading fluency) handicaps the pair-programming and code-review rounds - switch early. Thrive's window is one-shot (second-year only, fall deadline): a sophomore who learns about it in spring has already missed that cycle. Pittsburgh relocation is required for Thrive and HQ-centred onboarding - a real constraint, not a remote programme. Do not quote Glassdoor median-pay figures as Duolingo compensation facts; they are anonymous self-reports (Doc 3 s6 labelling rule). Adjacent options with similar signal: the other employers and role families whose CIRs share this ladder — the first rung matters more than the logo on it.

Want me to execute? I can build the coffee-chat target list from these routes, tailor your resume to this record's revealed screens (truthfully — only what you have actually done), and set the plan's reminders. Say the word and I start with the list.
